notes: A DO calibration whose inputs are three other metrics — temperature, barometric pressure and conductivity — and whose governing document changes in turn 2. USGS side: do-one-point-goal-01 (create a 100 percent saturated environment with sensor and thermistor at the same temperature), do-proc1-read-precision-01 (pressure to the nearest 1 mmHg, temperature to 0.1 C), do-water-droplets-01 and do-wet-towel-bag-shade-01, do-calibration-corrections-01 and do-auto-salinity-correction-01 / do-auto-salinity-multiparameter-01 (ionic strength estimated from the conductivity sensor, corrected automatically unless switched off), do-salinity-correction-after-01 (the preferred USGS method applies salinity factors AFTER calibration and measurement), do-manual-salinity-recalibration-01 (a manual salinity correction at calibration forces recalibration for every field salinity change), do-temp-controls-solubility-01. A6.8 supplies the record: mp-form-do-columns-05 lists exactly what the DO calibration block captures — calibration temperature, barometric pressure in mm Hg, table reading, salinity correction factor, DO before and after adjustment; mp-t4-nist-thermometer-02 makes the barometer NIST-traceable. Turn 2 moves to the EPA SOP, which prescribes a different cadence and a different check: epa-cal-frequency-daily-01, epa-post-cal-end-of-day-01, epa-midday-check-qualify-01 (only data before a failed midday check needs qualifying), epa-sonde-deploy-cal-01 (deployed sondes are calibrated before deployment and checked on recovery), epa-postcal-do-steps-01 and epa-oxygen-solubility-chart-01 / epa-do-solubility-20c-01 (the post-calibration DO check is read against an oxygen-solubility chart at the measured temperature and barometric pressure), epa-do-dry-sensor-01, epa-postcal-defaults-apply-when-01 (the SOP's tabulated criteria apply only if the project QAPP has none). Neither file answers both turns. Predicted rag: the slice has no calibration content at all for any metric.

turns.content: I calibrate the oxygen sensor in air at the truck and then the pod goes into brackish water. What do I actually have to have right at the truck for that calibration to mean anything once it's in the water?

must_contain: states the goal of the one-point calibration is a 100 percent oxygen-saturated environment with the DO sensor and its temperature sensor at the same temperature
states barometric pressure must be read at the time of calibration, to the nearest 1 mm Hg, from a calibration-checked barometer
states temperature must be read to the nearest 0.1 C
states the reported concentration is computed from the sensor signal together with temperature and ionic strength, so the sensor is not measuring mg/L directly
states ionic strength for the salinity correction is estimated from the conductivity measurement
warns to check for water droplets on the optical module and on the temperature sensor after calibrating, and to recalibrate if any were present
states the USGS preference is to apply salinity correction factors after calibration and measurement rather than during calibration
notes that entering a manual salinity correction at calibration forces recalibration for each change in field salinity
must_not: invents a barometric pressure or temperature reading precision not in the manual
treats the DO sensor as reading mg/L directly with no computation from temperature and ionic strength
ignores salinity entirely at a brackish site
cites a probe datasheet accuracy figure in place of the calibration procedure

turns.content: The contract we're working under says follow the EPA field SOP, not the USGS one. Does that change how often I calibrate and what I do at the end of the day?

must_contain: states the EPA SOP requires calibration at minimum before use on the day the measurements are made
states the EPA SOP requires a post-calibration check at the end of the day to determine whether the instrument drifted
states that if a midday check shows drift the instrument can be recalibrated and only data taken before that check needs qualifying
states a continuously deployed sonde is calibrated before deployment and its calibration checked on recovery
states the DO post-calibration check is done in measurement mode, recording DO, temperature and barometric pressure for comparison against an oxygen-solubility chart
states the SOP's own drift criteria apply only when the project quality assurance plan does not specify its own
must_not: presents the EPA SOP as replacing the analytical methods it supplements
invents a numeric drift criterion not present in the SOP
answers the cadence question from the USGS chapters instead of the EPA SOP
claims the two documents disagree without support
